name: The Sphere Jamsil
summary: A glowing 7 m LED sphere by Seokchon Lake that turns into a free 3D media-art show after dark.
description: Installed in Songpa Naru Park on the south shore of Seokchon Lake, The Sphere is a spherical LED structure that screens looping 3D media-art content — abstract patterns, seasonal themes, and a few interactive pieces visitors can trigger by standing in front of sensors. It's unstaffed, free, and open around the clock, so it works as a 20-minute add-on to a lakeside walk rather than a destination in itself. It sits about 10 minutes on foot from Lotte World Tower/Seoul Sky and Lotte World Adventure, making it an easy free stop before or after either. Content quality gets mixed reviews from frequent visitors, but as a no-cost night-time photo op by the water it's an easy win.
highlights: 7 m spherical LED screen wrapped in real-time 3D media art
A few interactive content segments triggered by motion
Lakeside setting on Seokchon Lake's south shore (Songpa Naru Park)
10-minute walk to Lotte World Tower / Seoul Sky and Lotte World Adventure
tips: Go after sunset (from ~7pm in late September) — the screen barely registers in daylight
Loop the rest of Seokchon Lake before or after; it's a flat, stroller-friendly path
Some visitors find the content library a bit thin/repetitive — treat it as a quick free photo stop, not a headline attraction
Nearest exit is Seokchon Station (Line 8) Exit 8, about 9 minutes on foot

reviews.text: The 3D media art blends nicely with the lake scenery, and having interactive content that visitors can trigger makes it feel fresh.
The content library feels a bit thin for what was spent on it — worth a quick look, not a long visit.
"Quite impressive either way" — a pleasant surprise on a lakeside evening walk.

hours.note: Unstaffed outdoor installation; media-art screen is most visible after dark.

chuseok.note: Unstaffed outdoor sculpture in a public park — nothing to close for Chuseok.

name: Ground Seesaw Hannam
summary: A rotating photography/art exhibition hall in a Hannam-dong basement — currently a summer-themed photo show through Nov 2026.
description: Ground Seesaw is a small chain of exhibition halls in converted commercial basements, and the Hannam branch (below the Gourmet494 Hannam food hall) is one of its best-rated. The current show, a Sung Ryul photography exhibition called "Summer-Like Us," runs 30 Apr–22 Nov 2026, so it will be on throughout the trip window. Rooms are air-conditioned, wheelchair-accessible, and low-effort to walk through at your own pace — a good rainy-afternoon or midday-heat option that isn't a workshop or physical activity. It's a 10-minute walk from Hangangjin Station, so easy to pair with a Hannam-dong lunch or the boutiques nearby.
highlights: Current exhibit: Sung Ryul photography show "Summer-Like Us" (through 22 Nov 2026)
Self-paced walkthrough, fully indoors and air-conditioned
Located beneath Gourmet494 Hannam food hall — easy to combine with a meal

Pair with lunch or a coffee at Gourmet494 Hannam right upstairs

reviews.text: Really enjoyed the exhibition, and the gallery itself is well laid out and tidy.
A visitor who booked early bird tickets for "Summer-Like Us" said it was worth the wait until the end of summer to catch it.
One visitor compared it to a manga come to life — a gentle, healing kind of show.

name: Ground Seesaw Central
summary: Ground Seesaw's flagship hall by Seoul Station — a photography exhibition two minutes from the KTX/subway concourse.
description: The Central branch, three floors up in the Grand Central building opposite Seoul Station, is Ground Seesaw's biggest and most-reviewed space (over 3,700 blog posts). It currently runs "Pyogisik" (표기식), a photography exhibition, with a per-person ticket and a wheelchair-accessible, cloakroom-equipped gallery. Because it's steps from Seoul Station it slots neatly into a transit day or a rainy-day plan without a special trip, and — unusually for Seoul exhibition spaces — it stays open on public holidays including Chuseok. Reviewers compare the production quality to a proper multiplex-grade show rather than a pop-up.

name: Dialogue in the Dark Bukchon
subcategory: Sensory experience (guided tour in total darkness)
summary: A 100-minute guided walk through pitch-black rooms led by a blind guide — the globally franchised sensory-empathy exhibit, in Bukchon.
description: Dialogue in the Dark is an internationally franchised experience (running in dozens of cities since the 1980s) where small groups are led entirely by touch, sound and smell through simulated everyday spaces — a park, a market, a boat — by a visually-impaired guide, with zero light the whole way. It's seated/walking only, no climbing or exertion, and genuinely popular with adults: reviewers describe it as calming and perspective-shifting rather than a haunted-house scare. Sessions run every 15 minutes and last about 100 minutes, so it fills a relaxed midday slot in the Bukchon/Anguk area.
highlights: 100-minute guided walk through several pitch-dark simulated environments
Led personally by a visually-impaired guide — genuine two-way conversation, not a recording
Suitable for ages 8–70; no physical exertion, just walking and touch
Central Bukchon location, walkable from Anguk Station / Insadong
tips: Book a specific 15-minute-interval time slot online — arrive 15 minutes early
Closed Mondays and Tuesdays every week — plan for Sat 26 or Sun 27 during this trip
First-timers say it's better to go in with zero research/expectations — let the guide lead
Store bags/phones in the lockers provided; nothing is visible inside anyway

reviews.text: If it's your first time, go in with as little information as possible — a genuinely good experience once you settle in.
An enjoyable time that made me appreciate everyday sight and sound all over again.
Our road-master guide made it an experience we won't forget — just go in and enjoy every moment without looking anything up first.

price.note: Around ₩33,000 per adult (check the official site for exact child/group tiers).

hours.note: Timed entry every 15 min by reservation; last entry roughly 17:00-17:30 to finish the 100-min session by close.

chuseok.note: No Chuseok-specific closure found; it runs on its usual Wed-Sun schedule, so 24-26 Sep (Thu-Sat) are open and it's the regular Mon/Tue weekly closure that affects 28-29 Sep, not the holiday.

name: Kakao Friends Hongdae Flagship
summary: A three-floor Ryan-and-friends wonderland by Hongik Univ. Station — free to browse, packed with photo zones and character goods.
description: Kakao's flagship character store fills three floors right by Hongik University Station with oversized Ryan, Apeach and Muzi statues, seasonal photo sets, and the full range of stationery, plushies and homeware. It's a genuinely low-effort browse — no admission, no lines to enter — that works well for grandparents who just want to look and grandkids who want to shop. Kakao rotates collabs and pop-ups through the space regularly, so there's usually something new even for repeat visitors.

name: Gentle Monster Hongdae Flagship
summary: Korea's avant-garde eyewear brand's Hongdae flagship, where sunglasses are almost secondary to the rotating sculptural art installations.

It's free to walk through even if nobody buys anything, and it draws design-forward visitors as much as sunglass shoppers. A relaxed, air-conditioned browse that works well paired with the Hapjeong/Hongdae riverside walk.

name: Kyobo Book Centre Gwanghwamun
summary: Korea's original flagship bookstore, a basement-level maze at Gwanghwamun with long reading tables and a big English section.
description: Opened in 1981, Kyobo's Gwanghwamun flagship is the original branch of Korea's biggest bookstore chain, spanning the entire basement of the Kyobo Life Insurance building with long communal reading tables, a big English-language and travel section, stationery, and a famous wooden Kyobo Table quote ("사람은 책을 만들고, 책은 사람을 만든다"). It's an easy, air-conditioned, zero-pressure browse for a rainy afternoon or a break between sights, and it's directly connected underground to Gwanghwamun Station.

name: Shinsegae Food Market Dogok
summary: A sleek premium supermarket two minutes from Dogok Station — imported groceries, wine and food-court counters under one roof.
description: Shinsegae Food Market is the department-store chain's stand-alone gourmet-supermarket format, and the Dogok branch is a bright, well laid-out example just one subway stop from Seocho — imported and Korean groceries, a curated wine section, bakery, and several counter restaurants (a popular conveyor-belt sushi spot among them) sharing the same floor. It's a genuinely relaxing, air-conditioned browse for grocery-loving parents, and doubles as a practical stop for snacks, banchan, or a quick meal without committing to a full restaurant sit-down. Free parking makes it easy if renting a car for part of the trip.

name: MUJI Gangnam
summary: MUJI's four-floor Gangnam flagship, with a MUJI Diner and café inside — a calm, minimalist browse two blocks from Seocho.
description: Spread over four floors of the Pagoda Tower building, MUJI's Gangnam flagship is one of its largest Korean stores — clothing, homeware, stationery, travel goods and a full grocery section, plus an in-house MUJI Diner and café for a coffee break mid-browse. It's calm, quiet and low-effort by design, and it sits just 4 minutes from Gangnam Station, technically inside Seocho-gu, making it one of the closest shopping stops to the family's home base. A good rainy-day or need-a-quiet-hour option that doesn't require any advance planning.

name: The Hanoi Foot & Body, Cheongdam Le Ciel
summary: A spotless, 5.0-rated foot-and-body massage chain in Cheongdam — reservation-only, open 10am-midnight every day of the year.
description: The Hanoi Foot & Body is a fast-growing Vietnamese-style massage chain, and its Cheongdam Le Ciel branch (in the basement of an upscale apartment retail arcade) is one of its top-reviewed locations, with a perfect 5.0 score across 148 reviews. Rooms are private and immaculately clean, therapists average 20 years' experience, and every visit starts with a foot-soak and hand-wrap before the main treatment — genuinely zero-effort, lie-down relaxation rather than a spa circuit to navigate. It runs 365 days a year including all public holidays, which makes it an easy fit for a Chuseok-week visit.

name: Pokemon Mega Festa: Pikachu's Autumn Outing

name: Demon Slayer: Total Concentration Exhibition
summary: Demon Slayer's first Korea exhibition in a Seongsu warehouse — closes 27 Sep, so only 26–27 Sep of this trip catch it.
description: This is the Korean debut of the "Total Concentration" (전집중) Demon Slayer touring exhibition, set up inside S-Factory's Building D in Seongsu with recreated scenes, original art panels and exclusive merchandise. It's been running since 27 June 2026 and is scheduled to close on 27 September 2026 — right in the middle of the trip window, so it's only catchable on Saturday 26 or Sunday 27 September, not the Monday/Tuesday after. Reviews are more mixed than most entries in this guide (some found the production value underwhelming for the price), so it's best treated as a fan-driven pop-in rather than a must-see, timed for anyone in the group who's into the anime.

reviews.text: Went to the Demon Slayer exhibition and understood why some visitors called it disappointing — the production quality felt underwhelming for the price.
A fan who visited on a weekday said it was worth it for the calm, uncrowded viewing experience despite mixed word-of-mouth.
One visitor said it's a must for anyone who loved the Mugen Train and Infinity Castle films, primarily for the exclusive merchandise.
